summary: Targi is a tight two-player worker placement and card-drafting game where players place their two figures on a shared 5x5 grid to gather resources and tribe cards, aiming to build the most valuable set of tribe abilities. It's a dense, puzzly duel with very little downtime and constant tension over which grid spots to claim first.
praised: Rich combos from tribe card synergies
Quick turns keep both players engaged
High replayability for a small box
criticised: Can feel a bit mathy or dry for some
Early tribe card draws can feel imbalanced
Rules for the grid take a game or two to internalize

interaction.kind: blocking the limited outer action spaces the only other player also needs
interaction.detail: With just two players and a fixed ring of 16 action spaces, taking a spot you need also removes it from the one opponent who could otherwise use it, making spot-blocking a constant tactical concern. Even so, much of each turn is spent managing your own hand of cards and central grid of goods and tribe cards, which are private.

scoring.how_you_win: Place workers around the grid each round to gather goods and trade them for tribe cards; after a fixed number of rounds, whoever holds the highest total value of acquired tribe cards wins.
